## OB.2: Evaluar la influencia de la estructura (DAP y altura) del árbol hospedero sobre la riqueza, abundancia y composicion de las epífitas, controlando el efecto de la elevación.

Paquetes

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(car)
library(stringi)
library(lme4)
library(performance)
library(emmeans)
library(sjmisc)
library(sjPlot)
library(ggplot2)
library(vegan)
library(betapart)
library(MASS)
library(patchwork)
library(readr)
library(lubridate)
library(emmeans)
library(ggpubr)
library(geosphere)
library(stringr)
library(glmmTMB)
library(ggplot2)

```

base de datos

```{r}
#setwd("C:/Users/edith clemente arena/Desktop/EPIFITAS -GRADIENTE/treeline-epiphytes/treeline-epiphytes/Doble_filtro/DATA")

#----------------------------------------------------
# FOROFITOS CON EPIFITAS
#----------------------------------------------------

data <- read.csv(
  "./Doble_filtro/DATA/estrucPOBa.csv",
  header = TRUE,
  sep = ";",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    morphospe = iconv(morphospe,
                      from = "",
                      to = "UTF-8",
                      sub = ""),
    
    morphospe = gsub("\u00A0", " ", morphospe),

    morphospe = str_squish(morphospe)
  )
sort(unique(data$morphospe))##revisar las especies

# data <- read.csv(
#   "./Doble_filtro/Data/estrucPOBa.csv",
#   header = TRUE,
#   sep = ";",
#   stringsAsFactors = FALSE
# )

hospepi <- data %>%
  dplyr::select(
    plot,
    elevation,
    forof,
    morphospe,
    family,
    subplot,
    dap,
    height
  )

#----------------------------------------------------
# ARBOLES
#----------------------------------------------------

trees <- read.csv(
  "./Doble_filtro/DATA/treealtu.csv",
  header = TRUE,
  sep = ";",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)


# trees <- read.csv(
#   "./Doble_filtro/Data/treealtu.csv",
#   header = TRUE,
#   sep = ";",
#   stringsAsFactors = FALSE
# )

tree <- trees %>%
  dplyr::select(
    ï..plot,
    elevation,
    tagtree,
    family,
    subplot,
    NC,
    DBH,
    H
  )
 colnames(tree)[1]<-"plot"
#----------------------------------------------------
# RENOMBRAR VARIABLES DE ARBOLES
#----------------------------------------------------

tree2 <- tree %>%
  rename(
    forof = tagtree,
    dap = DBH,
    height = H
  )

#----------------------------------------------------
# RESUMEN DE EPIFITAS POR FOROFITO
#----------------------------------------------------

epi_por_arbol <- hospepi %>%
  group_by(forof) %>%
  summarise(
    presencia_epifitas = 1,
    riqueza = n_distinct(morphospe),
    abundancia_total = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#----------------------------------------------------
# UNIR TABLAS
#----------------------------------------------------

arboles <- tree2 %>%
  left_join(
    epi_por_arbol,
    by = "forof"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    presencia_epifitas = ifelse(is.na(presencia_epifitas), 0, presencia_epifitas),
    riqueza = ifelse(is.na(riqueza), 0, riqueza),
    abundancia_total = ifelse(is.na(abundancia_total), 0, abundancia_total)
  )



#----------------------------------------------------
# VERIFICAR
#----------------------------------------------------

str(arboles)

table(arboles$presencia_epifitas)

table(arboles$plot, arboles$presencia_epifitas)

```

### RIQUEZA modelos

```{r}
#preparacion de datos escalar var numericas y genero como factor 
arboles$dap_z <- scale(arboles$dap)
arboles$height_z <- scale(arboles$height)
arboles$elevation <- as.factor(arboles$elevation)
arboles$subplot <- as.factor(arboles$subplot)

#MODELOS CON INTERACCION
m_ric_nb1 <- glmmTMB(
  riqueza ~ dap_z * height_z +(1|subplot),
  family = nbinom2,
  data = arboles
)
summary(m_ric_nb1)
Anova(m_ric_nb1, type = "II")#importancia de cada variable #VIF
library(performance)
check_collinearity(m_ric_nb1)

#evaluar residuos con DHARMa
res_ric1 <- simulateResiduals(m_ric_nb1)
plot(res_ric1)
testUniformity(res_ric1)#Residuales compatibles con la distribución esperada
testDispersion(res_ric1)#No hay evidencia de sobre- o subdispersión
testZeroInflation(res_ric1)#No hay evidencia significativa de exceso de ceros

m_ric_nb2 <- glmmTMB(
  riqueza ~ dap_z * height_z +(1|elevation),
  family = nbinom2,
  data = arboles
)
summary(m_ric_nb2)
Anova(m_ric_nb2, type = "II")#importancia de cada variable #VIF
check_collinearity(m_ric_nb2)

#evaluar residuos con DHARMa
res_ric2 <- simulateResiduals(m_ric_nb2)
plot(res_ric2)
testUniformity(res_ric2)#Residuales compatibles con la distribución esperada
testDispersion(res_ric2)#No hay evidencia de sobre- o subdispersión
testZeroInflation(res_ric2)#No hay evidencia significativa de exceso de ceros(cerca al limite)

m_ric_nb3 <- glmmTMB(
  riqueza ~ dap_z * height_z  + (1 | elevation/subplot),
  family = nbinom2,
  data = arboles
)
summary(m_ric_nb3)
Anova(m_ric_nb3, type = "II")#importancia de cada variable #VIF
check_collinearity(m_ric_nb3)

#evaluar residuos con DHARMa
res_ric3 <- simulateResiduals(m_ric_nb3)
plot(res_ric3)
testUniformity(res_ric3)#Residuales compatibles con la distribución esperada
testDispersion(res_ric3)#No hay evidencia de sobre- o subdispersión
testZeroInflation(res_ric3)#No hay evidencia significativa de exceso de ceros

#MODELOS SIN INTERACCION 
m_ric_nb4 <- glmmTMB(
  riqueza ~ dap_z + height_z +(1|subplot),
  family = nbinom2,
  data = arboles
)
#VIF
check_collinearity(m_ric_nb4)

m_ric_nb5 <- glmmTMB(

#VIF
check_collinearity(m_ric_nb5)

m_ric_nb6 <- glmmTMB(

Anova(m_ric_nb5, type = "II")
```

Graficar

```{r}
#RIQUEZA
#DAP
#crear datos para prediccion
new_dap <- data.frame(
  dap_z = seq(
    min(arboles$dap_z),
    max(arboles$dap_z),
    length.out = 100
  ),
  height_z = 0
)
#obtener predicciones del modelo 
pred <- predict(
  m_ric_nb4,
  newdata = new_dap,
  type = "link",
  se.fit = TRUE,
  re.form = NA
)
#Calcular IC95%
new_dap <- new_dap %>%
  mutate(
    fit = exp(pred$fit),
    lwr = exp(pred$fit - 1.96 * pred$se.fit),
    upr = exp(pred$fit + 1.96 * pred$se.fit)
  )
#Volver a la escala original de DAP
dap_mean <- mean(arboles$dap)
dap_sd   <- sd(arboles$dap)

new_dap <- new_dap %>%
  mutate(
    dap = dap_z * dap_sd + dap_mean
  )
#graficar 
gA <- ggplot(arboles,
             aes(x = dap,
                 y = riqueza)) +

  geom_point(
    alpha = 0.6,
    size = 2,
    color = "black"
  ) +

  geom_ribbon(
    data = new_dap,
    aes(x = dap,
        ymin = lwr,
        ymax = upr),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    alpha = 0.25
  ) +

  geom_line(
    data = new_dap,
    aes(x = dap,
        y = fit),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "DBH (cm)",
    y = "Epiphyte species richness"
  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 13)
gA

#altura
#----------------------------------------
# DATOS PARA PREDICCION
#----------------------------------------

new_height <- data.frame(
  dap_z = 0,  # DAP promedio
  height_z = seq(
    min(arboles$height_z),
    max(arboles$height_z),
    length.out = 100
  )
)

#----------------------------------------
# PREDICCIONES DEL MODELO
#----------------------------------------

pred <- predict(
  m_ric_nb4,
  newdata = new_height,
  type = "link",
  se.fit = TRUE,
  re.form = NA
)

#----------------------------------------
# INTERVALOS DE CONFIANZA
#----------------------------------------

new_height <- new_height %>%
  mutate(
    fit = exp(pred$fit),
    lwr = exp(pred$fit - 1.96 * pred$se.fit),
    upr = exp(pred$fit + 1.96 * pred$se.fit)
  )

#----------------------------------------
# VOLVER A ESCALA ORIGINAL (m)
#----------------------------------------

height_mean <- mean(arboles$height)
height_sd <- sd(arboles$height)

new_height <- new_height %>%
  mutate(
    height = height_z * height_sd + height_mean
  )

#----------------------------------------
# GRAFICO
#----------------------------------------

gB <- ggplot(arboles,
             aes(x = height,
                 y = riqueza)) +

  geom_point(
    alpha = 0.6,
    size = 2,
    color = "black"
  ) +

  geom_ribbon(
    data = new_height,
    aes(
      x = height,
      ymin = lwr,
      ymax = upr
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    alpha = 0.25
  ) +

  geom_line(
    data = new_height,
    aes(
      x = height,
      y = fit
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Tree height (m)",
    y = " "
  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 13)

gB
```

## Composición

¿Qué variables del forófito explican la composición de epífitas? dbRDA (capscale)

Data

```{r}

# =====================================================
# 1. MATRIZ DE COMUNIDAD POR FORÓFITO
# =====================================================

ABUNDFO <- data %>%
  group_by(forof, morphospe) %>%
  summarise(ABUNDANCIA = n(), .groups = "drop")

matrizf <- ABUNDFO %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = morphospe,
    values_from = ABUNDANCIA,
    values_fill = 0
  )

# corregir encoding inmediatamente
colnames(matrizf) <- iconv(
  colnames(matrizf),
  from = "",
  to = "UTF-8",
  sub = ""
)

colnames(matrizf) <- gsub(
  "\u00A0",
  " ",
  colnames(matrizf)
)

matriz_forof <- matrizf %>%
  group_by(forof) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), sum)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

rownames(matriz_forof) <- matriz_forof$forof
matriz_forof$forof <- NULL

# ==============================================
# 2. VARIABLES AMBIENTALES
# ==============================================

metadata <- data %>%
  group_by(forof) %>%
  summarise(
    plot = unique(plot),
    elevation = unique(elevation),
    subplot = unique(subplot),
    genera_tree = unique(genera_tree),
    dap = unique(dap),
    height = unique(height),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

```

```{r}
comm <- matriz_forof

# Recommended model set
# 
# Use these three models depending on the exact question:
# 
# 1. Total environmental/site structure
mod_site <- capscale(
  comm ~ plot,
  data = env,
  distance = "chao"
)
anova(mod_site)
RsquareAdj(mod_site)

# Question answered:
# Do epiphyte communities differ among plots/localities/elevations?
#Rpta: La composición de las comunidades de epífitas difiere significativamente entre localidades/elevaciones.
#Epiphyte community composition differed significantly among localities/elevations (dbRDA: F = 15.52, p = 0.001), with localities/elevations identity explaining 19.1% of the variation in community composition (adjusted R² = 0.191).

# 
# 2. Host-tree variables without accounting for plot
mod_host_simple <- capscale(
  comm ~ dap + height,
  data = env,
  distance = "chao"
)
anova(mod_host_simple)
anova(mod_host_simple, by = "term")
librRsquareAdj(mod_host_simple)

# Question answered:
# Are DAP and height associated with epiphyte composition overall?
#Rpta:Existe una asociación significativa entre las características del hospedero y la composición de epífitas.pero es pequeña Adjusted R² = 0.046 porque DAP y altura tienen un efecto detectable, pero explican solo alrededor del 4.6% de la variación total.
#Host-tree diameter (DAP) and height were significantly associated with epiphyte community composition (overall model: F = 5.41, p = 0.001), although together they explained a relatively small fraction of the variation (adjusted R² = 0.046).

# 3. Host-tree variables after controlling for plot
mod_host_controlled <- capscale(
  comm ~ dap + height + Condition(subplot),
  data = env,
  distance = "chao"
)
anova(mod_host_controlled)
anova(mod_host_controlled, by = "term")
anova(mod_host_controlled, by = "margin")
RsquareAdj(mod_host_controlled)
#question answered:
#Are the host -tree variables after controlling for "plot" associated with epiphyte composition ?
#Rpta: Sí Incluso después de controlar estadísticamente el efecto del plot, DAP y altura siguen siendo significativos. La relación entre las características del hospedero y la composición de epífitas no se debe simplemente a diferencias espaciales entre plots.
# Modelo                            | Adj. R² | #--------------------------------- | ------: |
# DAP + Height                      |  0.0455 |
# DAP + Height + Condition(subplot) |  0.0458 |
#Son prácticamente idénticos.Eso indica que el efecto de DAP y altura es bastante robusto y no depende mucho de la estructura espacial representada por el subplot
#The effects of DAP and host height remained significant after accounting for plot identity (F = 5.45, p = 0.001), indicating that host-tree characteristics influence epiphyte composition independently of local spatial structure.
```

para el dbRDA deberia usar el modelo comm \~ dap + height + Condition(subplot) ¿DAP y altura están asociados con la composición de epífitas independientemente de la estructura espacial local (subplot)?

```{r}
# ==============================================
# 3. dbRDA
# ==============================================

comm <- matriz_forof

env  <- metadata

mod <- capscale(
  comm ~ dap + height + Condition(subplot),
  data = env,
  distance = "chao"
)


mod_full <- capscale(
  comm ~ dap + height + genera_tree + Condition(subplot),
  data = env,
  distance = "chao"
)


# ==============================================
# 4. SIGNIFICANCIA
# ==============================================

anova(mod)
anova(mod, by = "term")
summary(mod)
RsquareAdj(mod)


anova(mod_full)
anova(mod_full, by = "term")
summary(mod_full)
RsquareAdj(mod_full)

# ==============================================
# 5. COORDENADAS DE LOS SITIOS
# ==============================================

coords <- as.data.frame(
  scores(mod, display = "sites")
)

coords$plot <- env$plot


coords_full <- as.data.frame(
  scores(mod_full, display = "sites")
)

coords_full$plot <- env$plot

# ==============================================
# 6. CENTROIDES
# ==============================================

centroides <- coords %>%
  group_by(plot) %>%
  summarise(
    CAP1 = mean(CAP1),
    CAP2 = mean(CAP2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


centroides_full <- coords_full %>%
  group_by(plot) %>%
  summarise(
    CAP1 = mean(CAP1),
    CAP2 = mean(CAP2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ==============================================
# 7. VARIABLES AMBIENTALES
# ==============================================

fit <- envfit(
  mod,
  env[, c("dap", "height")],
  permutations = 999
)


fit_full <- envfit(
  mod_full,
  env[, c("dap", "height", "genera_tree")],
  permutations = 999
)


# Direcciones de las flechas
ar <- fit$vectors$arrows

ar_full <- fit_full$vectors$arrows

# Fuerza de correlación
r <- sqrt(fit$vectors$r)

r_full <- sqrt(fit_full$vectors$r)

# Flechas escaladas según la correlación
ar_df <- data.frame(
  var  = rownames(ar),
  xend = ar[,1] * r * 3,
  yend = ar[,2] * r * 3
)

# Cambiar nombres
ar_df <- ar_df %>%
  mutate(
    var = dplyr::recode(
      var,
      dap = "DBH",
      height = "Height"
    )
  )


# Flechas escaladas según la correlación
ar_df_full <- data.frame(
  var  = rownames(ar_full),
  xend = ar[,1] * r * 3,
  yend = ar[,2] * r * 3
)

# Cambiar nombres
ar_df_full <- ar_df_full %>%
  mutate(
    var = dplyr::recode(
      var,
      dap = "DBH",
      height = "Height",
      genera_tree = "Genera"
    )
  )
# =====================================================
# 8. RENOMBRAR LOCALIDADES
# =====================================================

plot_names <- c(
  "TRU-02" = "FORST-3200",
  "TRU-01" = "TLINE-3400",
  "ACJ-01" = "TLINE-3500",
  "APK-01" = "TLINE-3600"
)

coords$plot_new <- plot_names[coords$plot]
centroides$plot_new <- plot_names[centroides$plot]


coords_full$plot_new <- plot_names[coords_full$plot]
centroides_full$plot_new <- plot_names[centroides_full$plot]

# =====================================================
# 9. COLORES
# =====================================================

colores_localidad <- c(
  "FORST-3200" = "#006400",
  "TLINE-3400" = "#A2CD5A",
  "TLINE-3500" = "#DAA520",
  "TLINE-3600" = "#8B4513"
)



# Flechas de las variables numéricas del modelo full
ar_full <- fit_full$vectors$arrows
r_full  <- sqrt(fit_full$vectors$r)

ar_df_full <- data.frame(
  var  = rownames(ar_full),
  xend = ar_full[, 1] * r_full * 3,
  yend = ar_full[, 2] * r_full * 3
)

ar_df_full$var <- dplyr::recode(
  ar_df_full$var,
  dap = "DBH",
  height = "Height"
)

# Centroides de los géneros
centros_generos <- fit_full$factors$centroids

generos_df <- data.frame(
  genero = sub("^genera_tree", "", rownames(centros_generos)),
  CAP1 = centros_generos[, 1],
  CAP2 = centros_generos[, 2]
)

# ==============================================
# 10. FIGURA FINAL
# ==============================================
library(ggrepel)
dbRDA_plot <- ggplot() +

  geom_point(
    data = coords,
    aes(CAP1, CAP2, fill = plot_new),
    shape = 21,
    color = "black",
    size = 3
  ) +

  geom_text_repel(
    data = centroides,
    aes(CAP1, CAP2, label = plot_new),
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 5,
    segment.color = NA,
    box.padding = 0.4,
    point.padding = 0.3,
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +

  geom_segment(
  data = ar_df,
  aes(
    x = 0,
    y = 0,
    xend = xend,
    yend = yend
  ),
  arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm")),
  linewidth = 1.2,
  color = "red"
) +

geom_text(
  data = ar_df,
  aes(
    x = xend * 1.10,
    y = yend * 1.10,
    label = var
  ),
  color = "red",
  fontface = "bold",
  size = 5
) +

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dotted",
    color = "grey50"
  ) +

  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dotted",
    color = "grey50"
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = colores_localidad
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "CAP1",
    y = "CAP2",
    fill = "Locality"
  ) +

  coord_equal() +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +

  theme(
    #panel.border = element_rect(
     # colour = "black",
      #fill = NA,
      #linewidth = 1
    #),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(
      colour = "grey85",
      linewidth = 0.3
    )
  )
dbRDA_plot

dbRDA_plot2 <- dbRDA_plot +##PARA hacerlo cuadrado
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(-4.5, 4.5)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(-4.5, 4.5)
  )

dbRDA_plot2
# ==============================================
# 11. EXPORTAR FIGURA
# ==============================================

ggsave(
  "dbRDA_epifitas3.png",
  plot = dbRDA_plot,
  width = 7,

)

summary(mod)
all(rownames(matriz_forof) == metadata$forof)

# 10. FIGURA FINAL full/genera
# ========================================
```

The dbRDA model was significant (F = 11.60, p = 0.001).

Environmental variables explained 24.4% of the variation in epiphyte community composition (adjusted R² = 0.223).

Elevation had the strongest effect on community composition, followed by plot identity, host-tree diameter (DAP), and host height (all p = 0.001).

The first two constrained axes explained 68.9% of the constrained variation.

Adding climate:

```{r}


library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(vegan)
library(permute)

# ============================================================
# 1. CLIMA: seleccionar puntos_interes_clima_30m.dbf
# ============================================================

clima <- foreign::read.dbf(file.choose(), as.is = TRUE)

bio_vars <- paste0("bio", 1:19)

equivalencias <- data.frame(
  plot = c("TRU-02", "TRU-01", "ACJ-01", "APK-01"),
  nombre = c(
    "FORST-3200", "TLINE-3400",
    "TLINE-3500", "TLINE-3600"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

stopifnot(
  all(c("nombre", bio_vars) %in% names(clima)),
  !anyDuplicated(clima$nombre)
)

clima_plot <- equivalencias %>%
  dplyr::left_join(clima, by = "nombre") %>%
  dplyr::select(plot, nombre, dplyr::all_of(bio_vars))

stopifnot(
  all(vapply(clima_plot[bio_vars], is.numeric, logical(1))),
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(clima_plot[bio_vars])))
)

# ============================================================
# 2. IDENTIFICAR CADA SUBPARCELA
# ============================================================

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(data[, c("plot", "subplot", "forof", "morphospe")])
)

datos <- data %>%
  mutate(
    plot = as.character(plot),
    subplot_id = paste(plot, subplot, sep = "_")
  )

# Número de árboles y registros disponibles por subparcela
esfuerzo <- datos %>%
  group_by(plot, subplot, subplot_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_arboles = n_distinct(forof),
    n_registros = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(plot, subplot)

print(esfuerzo)

# Comprobar cuatro localidades, con dos subparcelas cada una
stopifnot(
  nrow(esfuerzo) == 8L,
  n_distinct(esfuerzo$plot) == 4L,
  all(table(esfuerzo$plot) == 2L)
)

# ============================================================
# 3. MATRIZ: SUBPARCELAS × ESPECIES
#    Mantiene tu definición de abundancia: número de registros
# ============================================================

abund_subplot <- datos %>%
  count(subplot_id, morphospe, name = "abundancia")

matriz_subplot <- abund_subplot %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = morphospe,
    values_from = abundancia,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()

rownames(matriz_subplot) <- matriz_subplot$subplot_id
matriz_subplot$subplot_id <- NULL

# Metadatos y clima de cada subparcela
env_subplot <- esfuerzo %>%
  left_join(clima_plot, by = "plot") %>%
  arrange(plot, subplot) %>%
  mutate(plot = factor(plot))

# Alinear exactamente las filas
comm_subplot <- as.matrix(
  matriz_subplot[env_subplot$subplot_id, , drop = FALSE]
)

storage.mode(comm_subplot) <- "numeric"

stopifnot(
  identical(rownames(comm_subplot), env_subplot$subplot_id),
  all(rowSums(comm_subplot) > 0),
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(env_subplot[bio_vars])))
)

dim(comm_subplot)
View(comm_subplot)
View(env_subplot)

# ============================================================
# 4. PERMUTACIONES ENTRE LOCALIDADES
#    Cada pareja de subparcelas se mueve como un bloque.
#    No se permutan las subparcelas dentro de cada pareja.
# ============================================================

control <- how(
  within = Within(type = "none"),
  plots = Plots(
    strata = env_subplot$plot,
    type = "free"
  ),
  complete = TRUE,
  maxperm = 999
)

permutaciones <- as.matrix(
  allPerms(nrow(env_subplot), control = control)
)

# Eliminar la identidad si estuviera incluida
identidad <- seq_len(nrow(env_subplot))

permutaciones <- permutaciones[
  apply(permutaciones, 1, function(x) any(x != identidad)),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Deben quedar 23 ordenamientos distintos del observado
print(nrow(permutaciones))
stopifnot(nrow(permutaciones) == 23L)

# ============================================================
# 5. DISTANCIA CHAO ENTRE SUBPARCELAS
# ============================================================

dist_subplot <- vegdist(comm_subplot, method = "chao")

stopifnot(all(is.finite(dist_subplot)))

# ============================================================
# 6. UN CAPScale POR VARIABLE CLIMÁTICA
# ============================================================

modelos_clima <- setNames(
  vector("list", length(bio_vars)),
  bio_vars
)

resultados_lista <- vector("list", length(bio_vars))

for (i in seq_along(bio_vars)) {

  variable <- bio_vars[i]
  x <- env_subplot[[variable]]

  # Una variable constante no se puede evaluar
  if (length(unique(x)) < 2L) {
    resultados_lista[[i]] <- data.frame(
      variable = variable,
      R2 = NA_real_,
      F = NA_real_,
      p = NA_real_
    )
    next
  }

  formula_clima <- reformulate(
    variable,
    response = "dist_subplot"
  )

  modelo <- capscale(
    formula_clima,
    data = env_subplot,
    add = TRUE
  )

  prueba <- anova(
    modelo,
    permutations = permutaciones
  )

  modelos_clima[[variable]] <- modelo

  resultados_lista[[i]] <- data.frame(
    variable = variable,
    R2 = unname(RsquareAdj(modelo)$r.squared),
    F = prueba[1, "F"],
    p = prueba[1, "Pr(>F)"]
  )
}

# Ordenar por asociación con la composición
resultados_clima <- dplyr::bind_rows(resultados_lista) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    porcentaje_explicado = 100 * R2,
    p_Holm = p.adjust(p, method = "holm")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(R2)) %>%
  dplyr::select(variable, porcentaje_explicado, R2, F, p, p_Holm)

print(as.data.frame(resultados_clima), row.names = FALSE)
View(resultados_clima)

# ============================================================
# 7. GRÁFICO: VARIABLES ORDENADAS POR VARIACIÓN EXPLICADA
# ============================================================

grafico <- resultados_clima %>%
  filter(!is.na(R2)) %>%
  arrange(R2)

op <- par(mar = c(5, 6, 3, 1))

barplot(
  grafico$porcentaje_explicado,
  names.arg = grafico$variable,
  horiz = TRUE,
  las = 1,
  col = "#387D78",
  border = NA,
  xlab = "Variación en composición explicada (%)",
  main = "Asociación individual de las variables climáticas"
)

par(op)

# ============================================================
# 8. CORRELACIONES CLIMÁTICAS
#    Calcular sobre las cuatro localidades, sin duplicarlas.
# ============================================================

cor_clima <- cor(
  as.matrix(clima_plot[, bio_vars]),
  method = "pearson"
)

View(round(cor_clima, 2))

# Correlaciones entre las cinco variables mejor clasificadas
top5 <- head(
  resultados_clima$variable[!is.na(resultados_clima$R2)],
  5
)

print(round(cor_clima[top5, top5, drop = FALSE], 2))

# ============================================================
# 9. INSPECCIONAR EL MODELO CON MAYOR R²
# ============================================================

mejor_variable <- resultados_clima$variable[
  which.max(resultados_clima$R2)
]

mejor_modelo <- modelos_clima[[mejor_variable]]

cat("\nVariable con mayor asociación:", mejor_variable, "\n")

summary(mejor_modelo)

anova(
  mejor_modelo,
  permutations = permutaciones
)
```

```{r}

# ============================================================
# 8. PRUEBA WITHIN VS ACROSS
#    Unidad de reasignación: plot completo
# ============================================================

# Identificadores de los ocho plots de muestreo
plots_test <- meta_beta %>%
  dplyr::distinct(parcela, plot) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(parcela)

stopifnot(
  nrow(plots_test) == 8L,
  !anyDuplicated(plots_test$parcela),
  length(unique(plots_test$plot)) == 4L,
  all(table(plots_test$plot) == 2L)
)

# Las 28 combinaciones de ocho plots tomados de dos en dos
comparaciones <- resumen_plots %>%
  dplyr::filter(parcela_a != parcela_b) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    i = match(parcela_a, plots_test$parcela),
    j = match(parcela_b, plots_test$parcela)
  )

componentes <- c("beta_total", "turnover", "nestedness")

stopifnot(
  nrow(comparaciones) == choose(8, 2),
  !anyNA(comparaciones[, c("i", "j")]),
  !anyDuplicated(paste(
    pmin(comparaciones$i, comparaciones$j),
    pmax(comparaciones$i, comparaciones$j)
  )),
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(comparaciones[, componentes])))
)

# Grupos observados: las cuatro localidades
grupo_observado <- as.character(plots_test$plot)

# Diferencia de medias, dando igual peso a cada pareja de plots
calcular_delta <- function(grupos, valores) {

  within <- grupos[comparaciones$i] ==
            grupos[comparaciones$j]

  mean(valores[!within]) - mean(valores[within])
}

# ============================================================
# 9. GENERAR LAS 105 AGRUPACIONES EN CUATRO PAREJAS
# ============================================================

generar_parejas <- function(ids) {

  if (length(ids) == 0L) {
    return(list(matrix(integer(0), ncol = 2)))
  }

  primero <- ids[1]
  resultado <- list()

  for (segundo in ids[-1]) {

    restantes <- ids[!ids %in% c(primero, segundo)]
    colas <- generar_parejas(restantes)

    for (cola in colas) {
      resultado[[length(resultado) + 1L]] <-
        rbind(c(primero, segundo), cola)
    }
  }

  resultado
}

agrupaciones <- generar_parejas(seq_len(nrow(plots_test)))

stopifnot(length(agrupaciones) == 105L)

# Convertir cada agrupación en un vector de cuatro grupos
grupos_nulos <- lapply(agrupaciones, function(parejas) {

  grupos <- integer(nrow(plots_test))

  for (k in seq_len(nrow(parejas))) {
    grupos[parejas[k, ]] <- k
  }

  grupos
})

# ============================================================
# 10. PRUEBA EXACTA PARA CADA COMPONENTE
#     Alternativa unilateral: across > within
# ============================================================

resultados_test <- lapply(componentes, function(componente) {

  valores <- comparaciones[[componente]]

  within_obs <- grupo_observado[comparaciones$i] ==
                grupo_observado[comparaciones$j]

  delta_obs <- calcular_delta(grupo_observado, valores)

  delta_nulo <- vapply(
    grupos_nulos,
    function(g) calcular_delta(g, valores),
    numeric(1)
  )

  # Enumeración completa, incluida la agrupación observada:
  # no se añade +1 porque ya está incluida.
  p_exacto <- mean(delta_nulo >= delta_obs - 1e-12)

  data.frame(
    componente = componente,
    media_within = mean(valores[within_obs]),
    media_across = mean(valores[!within_obs]),
    delta = delta_obs,
    p = p_exacto,
    n_agrupaciones = length(delta_nulo)
  )
})

test_within_across <- dplyr::bind_rows(resultados_test) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    p_Holm = p.adjust(p, method = "holm")
  )

print(as.data.frame(test_within_across), row.names = FALSE)
View(test_within_across)

```
